explanations.answer: Only that He said He was their king
explanations.explanation: That's it. The chief priests tell Pilate: "Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but only that He said, ‘I am the King of the Jews.’…" See the little shift? They want the sign to say He claimed it, instead of stating it as the title. Good eye, baker.

explanations.answer: That His followers named Him their king
explanations.explanation: Close in sound, but that's not what they ask for. The chief priests say: "Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but only that He said, ‘I am the King of the Jews.’…" They want it to say that He said it Himself. John doesn't mention His followers in this request.

explanations.answer: That the crowds hailed Him as their king
explanations.explanation: Not quite. John records the request as: "Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but only that He said, ‘I am the King of the Jews.’…" The chief priests want the words to be His claim, not a crowd's cheer. No crowds come into this request at all.
